All this discussion is rather abstract.
It can be made much more concrete by moving to a convenient matrix representation known as the Kronecker product.
Suppose $A$ is an $m$ by $n$ matrix, and $B$ is a $p$ by $q$ matrix.
Then we have the matrix representation:

$$
A \otimes B \equiv \overbrace{\left[\begin{array}{cccc}
A_{11} B & A_{12} B & \ldots & A_{1 n} B  \tag{2.50}\\
A_{21} B & A_{22} B & \ldots & A_{2 n} B \\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots \\
A_{m 1} B & A_{m 2} B & \ldots & A_{m n} B
\end{array}\right]}^{n q}\} m p
$$

In this representation terms like $A_{11} B$ denote $p$ by $q$ submatrices whose entries are proportional to $B$, with overall proportionality constant $A_{11}$.
